'''Justin Williams''' (born May 12, 1984) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He is a {{height|ft=6|in=10}}, {{convert|260|lbs|kg}} [[power forward]]-[[Center (basketball)|center]].

==High school==
Born in [[Chicago, Illinois]], Williams attended [[Thornwood High School]], in [[South Holland, Illinois]], where he played high school basketball.

==College career==
Williams played [[college basketball]] the [[Colby Community College]], from 2002 to 2004, and at the [[University of Wyoming]], with the [[Wyoming Cowboys basketball|Wyoming Cowboys]], from 2004 to 2006.

==Professional career==
Williams went undrafted by an NBA team and started to play with the [[NBA Development League]]'s [[Dakota Wizards]], averaging 12.1 points, 12.3 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and 3.08 blocks in 12 games. He was signed by the [[Sacramento Kings]] to a first 10-day contract on January 5, 2007.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/kings/news/Kings_Sign_Justin_Williams_010507.html Kings Sign Justin Williams]</ref>  After the Kings released [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] [[Maurice Taylor]] on January 23, Williams was signed for the rest of season after his two 10-day contracts expired.

On February 16, 2008, Williams was waived by Sacramento together with teammate [[Dahntay Jones]] to make room for a trade that sent the Kings' veteran [[point guard]] [[Mike Bibby]] to the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. On March 7, he was signed by the [[Houston Rockets]] to a 10-day contract.<ref name=yahoo>{{Cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=txrocketsjwilliams&prov=st&type=lgns |title=Rockets sign C Justin Williams |access-date=January 14, 2017 |archive-date=March 12, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080312134435/http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=txrocketsjwilliams&prov=st&type=lgns |url-status=dead }}</ref> He played in one game for the Rockets.

Williams was brought to [[Golden State Warriors]] training camp on September 27, 2008,<ref>[http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors_sign_justin_williams.html Warriors Sign Justin Williams]</ref> but he was cut after appearing in two pre-season games.

On October 16, 2008, Williams was signed by the [[Charlotte Bobcats]]. But six days later, he was waived again after failing to impress in three pre-season games.<ref>[http://canadianpress.google.com/article/ALeqM5jaSug0wj4iuewJuQ9VrkS7VKnCCw Justin Williams is waived by Bobcats]{{dead link|date=November 2012|bot=Legobot}}</ref>

In 2012, Williams signed with the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] of the [[NBA D-League]]. He played in one game for the D-Fenders recording just one foul in two minutes of play.

In 2013, he was signed as an import for [[GlobalPort Batang Pier]] in the Philippines.<ref>[https://www.asia-basket.com/Philippines/basketball.aspx?NewsID=304037 Teams gearing up for 2013 PBA Commissioner's Cup]</ref> He was replaced midseason by [[Walter Sharpe]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.court-side.com/news/blog/walter-sharpe-moves-to-global-port/ |title=Walter Sharpe moves to Global Port |access-date=2013-03-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130321063136/http://www.court-side.com/news/blog/walter-sharpe-moves-to-global-port/ |archive-date=2013-03-21 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He later joined the [[San Miguel Beermen (ABL)|San Miguel Beermen]].<ref>[http://manilastandardtoday.com/2013/03/15/williams-suits-up-for-beermen/ Williams suits up for Beermen]{{Dead link|date=January 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===Argentine League===
Williams joined [[Club Ciclista Olímpico|Ciclista Olímpico]] for the 2015 Argentine league [[Liga Nacional de Básquet]].<ref>[https://www.laliganacional.com.ar/laliga/club/olimpico/page/noticias/id/4499/title/Justin-Williams,-nuevo-for%C3%A1neo-de-Ol%C3%ADmpico Justin Williams signs for Ciclista Olímpico]</ref>

===Titanes de Barranquilla (2021)===
In 2021, Williams played for the Colombian team [[Titanes de Barranquilla]] in the [[2021 BCL Americas]] season. He led the league in blocks with 2.8 blocks per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Players statistics of the Basketball Champions League Americas 2021 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/bclamericas/20-21/playerstats |website=FIBA.basketball |access-date=25 March 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

==Player profile==
Williams is best known for his shot-blocking and rebounding abilities. While playing for the University of Wyoming in the 2006 Mountain West Conference Tournament on March 11, he recorded a [[triple-double]] in a second-round game against the [[University of Utah]] with 10 points, 15 rebounds, and 12 blocked shots.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20181122055117/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=260692751 Wyoming 60, Utah 47]</ref>
In 2015, Williams lead the Argentine league in rebounds (11.2) and blocks (3.9).<ref>[http://www.pickandroll.com.ar/basquet/lnb/liga-a/2015-2016/individuales/?opci=destacados&modo=TAP&orde=DES&cant=50 Argentinean league individual stats]</ref>

==Sexual assault case==
On October 17, 2007, [[Sacramento, California|Sacramento]] police searched Williams' home in a northern Sacramento neighborhood.  The following day, at a press conference, a police spokesman indicated that they were conducting an ongoing [[sexual assault]] investigation, resulting from a young woman's appearance at a local hospital.<ref name=cpress>[http://canadianpress.google.com/article/ALeqM5j3UKaU84eTMBB6wp9uNAWNvMwsHg Sacramento police search home of Kings player in alleged assault] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071020101217/http://canadianpress.google.com/article/ALeqM5j3UKaU84eTMBB6wp9uNAWNvMwsHg |date=October 20, 2007 }}</ref>

Williams, who was traveling with the Sacramento Kings for an exhibition game in [[Albuquerque, New Mexico]], was put on a leave of absence and sent home in order to hire legal counsel.<ref name=cpress/> On November 13, 2007, Sacramento District Attorney Jan Scully concluded that Williams would not be charged for anything due to evidence not supporting the filing of any criminal charges in the case.<ref>[http://www.sacbee.com/102/v-print/story/489341.html D.A. says Kings' Justin Williams will not be charged in alleged sex assault case] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080117180205/http://www.sacbee.com/102/v-print/story/489341.html |date=2008-01-17 }}</ref>
